field_rule: Trace a complete mature flowering culm and locate the narrow sheath (spathe) surrounding each flowering raceme pair. This is a separately accepted Anatherum species historically called Andropogon glomeratus var. pumilus, not automatically true bushy bluestem (A. glomeratum). The current Linda Jo Conn image and Starr historical-variety images teach gross habit only. Do not certify the source photo or a Hays occurrence as this species from a fluffy head. Gallery 0 is the sole source-labelled original flowering image; panels 1, 4 and 5 are historical var. pumilus source views, not independent modern vouchers or measured anatomy.

diagnostic_checks.look: Open the inner ligule with a hand lens

diagnostic_checks.certainty: Taxon-concept-specific, not a standalone determination

diagnostic_checks.look: Measure the attached sessile spikelet

field_rule:
Flora field cue (Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, p. 1239) — Under Andropogon virginicus, the Flora describes usually straw-colored sheathing bracts around flowering branches 2–3 cm long. Follow several branches to see how they are spaced.

Follow one attached upper culm, not its winter color. Broomsedge is a warm-season tufted perennial; its narrow flowering units are commonly 2–5 short rames per spathe, mostly 1–3 cm long. Panel 1 shows gross flowering hairs, but cannot prove the number or attachment of individual rames.

head.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas pp.162–163 under Andropogon virginicus

diagnostic_checks.look: Follow several separate spathe-held flowering units
diagnostic_checks.check: Each upper culm bears separate straw-colored subtending spatheoles; within them, often 2–5 short, hairy rames around 2–3 cm, rather than one thick tight terminal brush.
diagnostic_checks.compare: bushy bluestem's denser corymbose flowering mass

head.reference: Annual brome with 8–20 florets in elongated spikelets and erect to open branching panicle; may appear contracted before maturity.

ligule.reference: Eciliate membrane, not a hair-only fringe.

diagnostic_checks.look: Measure the mature spikelet and floret count
diagnostic_checks.check: FNA describes 20–50 mm lanceolate spikelets bearing roughly 7–20 florets; spikelets often occur more than one at a branch node, and mature floret bases tend to conceal the rachilla internodes.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Texas brome has usually fewer florets, about 6–8, and shorter 20 mm spikelets
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA source checked; botanical macro pending

diagnostic_checks.look: Count glume veins and lemma size
diagnostic_checks.check: Lower glume normally 3–5-veined, upper 5–7-veined; mature lemmas about 11–20 mm, with 6–12 mm or occasionally longer diverging awns.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Texas brome lower glume usually one-veined, upper three-veined and 9–12 mm lemma
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA source checked; photograph with scale needed
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Bromus lanceolatus

diagnostic_checks.look: Follow a flowering stem to its ANNUAL base
diagnostic_checks.check: This introduced Mediterranean annual can have densely contracted young panicles opening later; flexible or stiff branch shape changes with stage. Do not use terminal panicle density as its only clue.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Other annual Bromus species; perennial hairy woodland brome
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA phenology checked; regional field voucher pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Bromus lanceolatus

ligule.source: USDA Forest Service, Lindheimer Panicum, https://www.srs.fs.usda.gov/pubs/rp/rp_so210.pdf (treatment as D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri)
ligule.reference: Description reports dense white HAIR-FRINGE ligule ~4–5 mm and small spring panicle 4–7 cm; source uses a different infraspecific taxon concept. Do not automatically merge identities.

name_concept.source: Kew POWO accepted D. lindheimeri; older US Forest Service D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri account
name_concept.reference: Names crosswalk, but historical floral/ligule measurements are under older variety concept; old identified photos must be independently linked to present accepted species concept.

diagnostic_checks.look: Look for the spring head, then its very different late leafy branching
diagnostic_checks.check: The U.S. Forest Service account (under D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri) describes a ~4–7 cm spring panicle with tiny spikelets and later low, spreading or prostrate stems crowded with small leaves. Do NOT automatically classify those late shoots as a different grass.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. commutatum also has spring/open and late reduced panicles; D. oligosanthes has larger spikelets and a more obvious winter rosette.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Season and historical taxon variety account; photo same-plant spring–fall sequence pending
diagnostic_checks.source: US Forest Service — Lindheimer Panicum (older variety name)

diagnostic_checks.look: Measure the TINY spikelets and white hair ligule
diagnostic_checks.check: Historical USFS treatment lists small ~1–2 mm spikelets and a dense true ring of white ligule hairs about 4–5 mm tall. Older regional acuminatum var. lindheimeri reports 1–2.1 mm spikelets; lower glume only about 1/4–1/2 spikelet in a broader D. acuminatum account.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. oligosanthes is much larger (typically 2.7–4.2 mm spikelets). Some other D. acuminatum group members also have tiny spikelets: hair length alone does not settle identity.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Taxon concept from D. acuminatum var./subsp. lindheimeri; not automatically all D. lindheimeri voucher populations
diagnostic_checks.source: US Forest Service — Lindheimer Panicum (older variety name)

diagnostic_checks.look: Record the exact name concept BEFORE confirming the specimen
diagnostic_checks.check: Kew accepts D. lindheimeri as a species but also records D. acuminatum subsp. lindheimeri and older Panicum lindheimeri. A specimen labeled with one of these may use a broader or narrower concept. Check tiny ligule, spikelet and stem/sheath hair together and record the source name.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. acuminatum and D. longiligulatum groups overlap in hair and spikelet measurements; current name by itself doesn't validate an old photo ID.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Accepted-name crosswalk secure; fine delimitation and winter rosette status not yet verified
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew POWO — Dichanthelium lindheimeri accepted name/synonyms

ligule.source: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas (1999), monocots excerpt pp.224 and 226, historical name Panicum pedicellatum
ligule.reference: Ligule hair fringe usually 0.3–1 mm, distinct from outer blade-edge hairs. Flowering may recur late summer and fall.

rootstock.source: UT Plant Resources Center, A.C. Gibson — Dichanthelium pedicellatum, Williamson County
rootstock.reference: Cormlike 5 x 3 mm shallow base with axillary buds and fibrous roots; NO basal winter rosette; each individual stem arises from a cormlike structure. Do not infer corm from fibrous roots alone.

diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect the underground CORM-LIKE base—don't demand a rosette
diagnostic_checks.check: Art Gibson's Williamson County treatment describes each slender stem rising from a shallow, covered, whitish CORM-LIKE swollen base up to ~5 × 3 mm bearing axillary buds and fibrous roots. It explicitly reports **NO basal rosette** for this species.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. oligosanthes has an authentic well-formed winter rosette; a detached basal stem or plain fibrous roots cannot confirm a corm.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: UT Williamson County specimen description, validated first PDF page; photograph of same-plant exposed corm still pending
diagnostic_checks.source: UT Plant Resources Center — Dichanthelium pedicellatum

diagnostic_checks.look: Measure the minute ligule separately from throat/outer hairs
diagnostic_checks.check: The TRUE ligule is a straight fringe of hairs only ~0.25–0.5 mm tall at the inner blade–sheath junction. Longer hairs with swollen bases line the blade margins near the collar. The narrow blade is typically 1.3–5.5 mm wide.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. lindheimeri has a much more obvious white hair ligule (~4–5 mm in the USFS older-name concept) and can have wider spring blades.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Directly read Williamson County description; true ligule not confirmed in current gallery macros
diagnostic_checks.source: UT Plant Resources Center — Dichanthelium pedicellatum

diagnostic_checks.look: Count the small spikelet glumes and its true two florets
diagnostic_checks.check: In Williamson County material, terminal panicles to 8 cm have 3–3.5 mm obovoid spikelets: lower glume ~1.5–2.1 mm ONE-veined; upper glume ~2.5–2.8 mm NINE-veined; lower sterile lemma ~2.4–2.8 mm with 7–9 veins and a lower palea; upper bisexual floret becomes hard.
diagnostic_checks.compare: D. oligosanthes spikelets can overlap in SIZE but lower glume often shorter (~1–1.6 mm FNA); corm, lack of basal rosette, and sheath anatomy are stronger combined checks.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Same Williamson County specimen; values may vary outside this population, use a scale and rooted voucher
diagnostic_checks.source: UT Plant Resources Center — Dichanthelium pedicellatum

diagnostic_review.note: Regional or older-taxonomy botanical sources checked; exact local specimen and seasonal gallery photo morphology remain unverified.

head.reference: Unlike typical digitate Digitaria, D. cognata has a much-branched very open panicle with spikelets on long pedicels, often detaching and tumbling.

ligule.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, uploaded monocots excerpt p.187
ligule.reference: Flora states the ligule is a membrane; Hays source notes a short erose membrane that remains unverified photographically.

diagnostic_checks.look: Trace a complete, widely branching flowering panicle
diagnostic_checks.check: Fall witchgrass produces a diffuse, wiry, spreading panicle with usually SOLITARY oval or lanceolate spikelets at ends of long pedicels. Mature branches may detach and tumble; a 'finger' cluster is not typical.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Southern crabgrass has 3–7(+) relatively straight racemes with *paired* crowded spikelets along their lower edges.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Texas A&M + Oklahoma State field accounts; whole-attached panicle photo needed
diagnostic_checks.source: Texas A&M — Fall witchgrass

diagnostic_checks.look: Look for a nearly absent LOWER glume
diagnostic_checks.check: Oklahoma State reports a lower glume tiny or absent, upper glume nearly as long as the lower sterile lemma. Each spikelet contains a sterile lower and fertile upper floret; this fits the panicoid pair, not a 4–13-flowered sprangletop spikelet.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Digitaria ciliaris instead has a distinct small triangular lower glume and short winged racemes carrying spikelets in pairs.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Oklahoma State floral account; close scaled floret anatomy pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Oklahoma State Plant ID — Digitaria cognata

diagnostic_checks.look: Separate crinkled leaf edge from inner ligule
diagnostic_checks.check: The short MEMBRANOUS ligule is at the blade–sheath junction. A white, often wavy or crinkled blade margin, densely hairy LOWER sheaths and a perennial wiry, horizontal stem base are useful together.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Southern crabgrass is generally annual, usually with somewhat broader leaves and a digitate seedhead; color and leaf-edge curl alone are insufficient.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Oklahoma State + Texas A&M vegetative treatment; no winter rooted voucher confirmed
diagnostic_checks.source: Oklahoma State Plant ID — Digitaria cognata

diagnostic_review.note: Taxon-source anatomical prompts, not confirmed local specimen dissection or verified exact diagnostic photograph.

head.source: Kew POWO GrassBase under Leptochloa panicea, https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:60458620-2/general-information
head.reference: Numerous slender straight ascending one-sided racemes along central axis, not clustered terminal fingers; subspecies-specific character unverified.

ligule.source: Kew POWO GrassBase under Leptochloa panicea, same source
ligule.reference: Eciliate membranous ligule described at species level; subspecies treatment requires separate crosswalk.

taxon_concept.source: Kew POWO Dinebra panicea / synonym Leptochloa panicea Flora of Tropical East Africa
taxon_concept.reference: Species-level panicea complex morphology can be applied to broad comparison but does not authenticate ssp. mucronata; needs local voucher and diagnostic subspecies treatment.

diagnostic_checks.look: Trace the numerous slender parallel flowering branches
diagnostic_checks.check: Kew's older *Leptochloa panicea* morphology gives a narrow, brushlike 9–36 cm head of many slender straight ascending unilateral branches, often 2–14 cm long, arranged along the central axis.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Green sprangletop (*Disakisperma dubium*) often has fewer, looser, outward-flexing branches and much larger spikelets.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Species-level old-name source; NOT independently proof of the subspecies mucronata
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew POWO / GrassBase under Leptochloa panicea

diagnostic_checks.look: Dissect a tiny MULTIFLORED spikelet
diagnostic_checks.check: The older species account gives a laterally compressed 1.8–2.5 mm spikelet with about 2–4(5) florets, unequal glumes ~0.9–1.7 mm and minute blunt two-toothed lemmas ~0.9–1.2 mm.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Green sprangletop typically has 4–13 florets but a much larger 4–12 mm spikelet and longer glumes; don't mistake a single spikelet for a whole branch.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Species-level old-name account; subspecies-level diagnostic characters remain unresolved
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew POWO — Dinebra panicea source under Leptochloa

diagnostic_checks.look: Check true ligule and record taxon concept
diagnostic_checks.check: A short membranous ligule, rather than a pure hair ring, and hairy sheath/blade may fit the broader Dinebra panicea complex. The published older name *Leptochloa panicea* must be crosswalked before claiming subsp. *mucronata*.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Disakisperma has a 0.5–1.5 mm ciliate membrane but differs more reliably in mature floral structures and hidden cleistogamous shoots.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Generic/species morphology source; do NOT mark exact subspecies verified without voucher treatment
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew POWO — Dinebra panicea accepted-name page

field_rule: STINKGRASS = annual with comparatively large dense multi-flowered spikelets, often with glandular pits. Smell alone isn't ID.
trait_provenance: Hays Botany Poaceae existing individual species lesson; provisional broad field-state coding; final GrassBase and North Central Texas flora comparison pending

habit.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, user-provided monocots excerpt, uploaded PDF p. 194
habit.reference: Flora confirms introduced annual and diagnostic lemma keel glands; existing partly open/compact and hair-ligule characters need closer FNA plus photo review.

diagnostic_checks.look: Search for the crater-like GLANDS, not just a smell
diagnostic_checks.check: Stinkgrass often has tiny wart/crater-like glands on spikelet lemma KEELS and/or glumes, branchlets, leaf margins, and sometimes in a ring below the culm nodes. Glands are variable and may be missing on some structures; do not declare all glandless plants different species.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Other lovegrasses have hair tufts but not usually this same combination of dense glandular spikelets and annual base.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Kew GrassBase and Flora Zambesiaca; gland expression variable and requires hand lens
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew GrassBase — Eragrostis cilianensis

diagnostic_checks.look: Count a larger number of florets in a broad spikelet
diagnostic_checks.check: Kew describes oblong or ovate compressed spikelets roughly 3–20 mm long, 2–4 mm wide, with 5–60 florets, and chartaceous ~2–2.8 mm lemmas sometimes glandular on the three-veined keel. Dense panicle may be open or contracted.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Hirsute/bigtop lovegrass usually has much tinier 2–4 mm, 2–6-flowered spikelets; red lovegrass can be many-flowered but perennial and usually not glandular.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: GrassBase range broad; photograph mature attached spikelets before confident ID
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew GrassBase — Eragrostis cilianensis

diagnostic_checks.look: Verify annual crown and true hair-fringe ligule
diagnostic_checks.check: A tufted ANNUAL with hair-fringe ligule near 0.5 mm; leaf/sheath surfaces and panicle branches may carry glands. Odor is a supporting cue but not an anatomical determination.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Purple and red lovegrasses are perennials; purple lovegrass can have knotty short rhizomes; rooted base plus glands better than color.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: Kew and World Flora Online; no locally rooted same-plant field photo certified
diagnostic_checks.source: Kew GrassBase — Eragrostis cilianensis
